[shr-00001] When the target object is not found in expected storage locations, continue systematically searching all relevant objects and receptacles until the object is located.
[shr-00006] When multiple true variants of the target object are found in the same receptacle, prioritize picking up the first one listed in the observation to minimize decision time and avoid unnecessary exploration.
[shr-00008] When multiple valid variants of the target object (as defined in [vc-00004]) are found in the same receptacle, prioritize picking up the first one listed in the observation to minimize decision time and avoid unnecessary exploration.
[shr-00010] When multiple valid variants of the target object (e.g., tissuebox 1, tissuebox 2, tissuebox 3) are found in the same receptacle, prioritize picking up the first one listed in the observation to minimize decision time and avoid unnecessary exploration.
[shr-00012] When multiple objects are found in a receptacle and one is a true variant of the target object (as defined in [vc-00005]), prioritize picking up the true variant over non-variant objects to ensure task correctness.
[shr-00015] When an object is found in a receptacle and the task requires it to be clean, and the object is not already clean, prioritize using a sinkbasin for cleaning it before proceeding to place it in the target receptacle.
[shr-00016] When an object needs to be clean and is moved to a sinkbasin for cleaning, explicitly perform a 'clean' action on the object using the sinkbasin and verify the object's state in the observation before proceeding to place it in the target receptacle.
[shr-00019] When an object is found in a receptacle that is not a sinkbasin and the task requires it to be clean, prioritize moving the object to a sinkbasin for cleaning before proceeding to place it in the target receptacle.
## VERIFICATION CHECKLIST
[vc-00002] When an object is moved to a target receptacle, confirm that the object is now listed as being on or in the receptacle in the observation.
[vc-00003] When revisiting a receptacle that has already been opened and inspected and found to not contain the target object, skip it to avoid redundant exploration.
[vc-00004] When a variant of the target object (e.g., soapbar instead of soapbottle) is found, consider it a valid candidate for the task and proceed to pick it up and place it on the target receptacle.
[vc-00005] When considering an object as a substitute for the target object, ensure it is a true variant (e.g., soapbar for soapbottle) and not a different type of object (e.g., spraybottle for soapbottle).
[vc-00007] When the target object is moved to the target receptacle and the observation confirms its presence there, consider the task complete and discontinue further exploration.
[vc-00009] When a variant of the target object is selected for placement, confirm that it is a true variant (e.g., tissuebox 3 for tissuebox) and not a different type of object (e.g., soapbar for tissuebox), as defined in [vc-00005].
[vc-00011] When the task requires an object to be in a specific condition (e.g., 'clean'), confirm that the object meets that condition before placing it in the target receptacle.
[vc-00013] When a true variant of the target object is found, verify that it meets the required condition (e.g., 'clean') before placing it in the target receptacle, as defined in [vc-00011].
[vc-00014] When an object is retrieved from a specific receptacle and the task does not specify a different target, consider placing it back in the same receptacle to maintain consistency and efficiency.
[vc-00017] When an object is moved to a sinkbasin for cleaning, confirm that the observation indicates the object is now clean (e.g., 'now clean') before proceeding to place it in the target receptacle.
[vc-00018] When placing an object in the target receptacle, confirm that it is both a true variant of the target object (as defined in [vc-00005]) and meets the required condition (e.g., 'clean') before proceeding.
